items.title: Mother braves flames thrice, but fails to save son from house fire
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: A mother braved raging flames three times in a desperate attempt to wake her sleeping son, but the rescue attempt ended in tragedy when he was found dead in a house fire at Kampung Gong Tok Nasek here, late last night. In the 10.50pm incident, Sharipah Yusof, 59, said she and her husband, Abd Rashid Md Zain, 64, were asleep downstairs, while her eldest son, Abd Latif Abd Rashid, 41, was sleeping alone in an upstairs bedroom. Sharipah said she braved the fire three times while knocking on her son's bedroom door, which was locked from the inside, but received no response.

items.title: Anwar praises Malaysian contingent’s fighting spirit at Glasgow Commonwealth Games
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated the entire Malaysian contingent for their fighting spirit and commendable performances at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games. In a Facebook post last night, he also expressed appreciation to the coaches, officials, support staff and all Malaysians who continuously prayed for the success of the national contingent. “Alhamdulillah, my heartfelt congratulations to the entire Malaysian contingent for competing with great pride and displaying extraordinary fighting spirit at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games.

items.title: Govt seeks wider gas supply options as Malaysia moves to boost energy security
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — The government is prioritising Malaysia’s energy security by diversifying access to large-scale gas resources that could broaden supply options and enhance the country’s energy resilience. The Economy Ministry said that amid uncertainty in global energy markets caused by geopolitical tensions, Malaysia remained focused on diversifying its energy supply sources to reduce reliance on any single country or market. Regarding opportunities to develop gas fields in Turkmenistan, the ministry said such ventures would be assessed based on their commercial merits and potential contribution to diversifying Malaysia’s long-term gas supply.

items.title: Democratic-led US states sue in latest challenge to Trump's tariffs
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Twenty-five US states, nearly all led by Democrats, sued Donald Trump's administration on Monday over wide-ranging tariffs, arguing that the president had exceeded his authority in imposing the new levies on dozens of countries. The states filed suit at the US Court of International Trade in New York, asking judges to halt the implementation of the tariffs, declare them unlawful and order the government to issue refunds. "There is no rational fit between the purported problem of forced labour in international supply chains and the blanket global tariffs the USTR imposed," the coalition of states argued in a court filing, referring to the US Trade Representative's office.

items.title: Maran Umno Youth chief, three family members buried in one grave
items.summary: The four victims — Radzi, his wife, Nuraini Mohammad Jafri, 36, their five-year-old son, Rizz Hazim, and Radzi's brother-in-law, Mohammad Nizam Mohammad Jafri, 34 — were buried at the Sri Chedung Muslim cemetery here about 3.15am. In the 12.30pm incident, Radzi, Nuraini, Rizz Hazim and Mohammad Nizam, who was driving the pick-up truck, were killed on the spot . Rizz Hazim's twin brother, Muhammad Rizz Haziq, survived with injuries.

items.title: KTMB expands Southern Shuttle route linking Paloh to JB Sentral from Aug 8
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) will extend its Southern Shuttle service on the Paloh-JB Sentral-Paloh route from Aug 8. KTMB said in a statement yesterday that the expanded service will cover seven stations—Paloh, Kluang, Renggam, Layang-Layang, Kulai, Kempas Baru and JB Sentral—with the journey from Paloh to JB Sentral taking about 120 minutes. KTMB said the new service will operate 10 trips daily, comprising five services from Paloh to JB Sentral and five in the opposite direction, with each train accommodating up to 400 passengers.

items.title: Malaysia, Cambodia to strengthen cooperation in AI, digital economy and cross-border crime, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — Malaysia and Cambodia have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening strategic cooperation across various sectors, including the digital economy, artificial intelligence (AI), the halal industry, food security and human capital development, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. In a Facebook post last night he said the commitment also encompassed efforts to enhance cooperation in combating cross-border crime. Anwar said the matter was discussed during a courtesy call by Cambodian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Prak Sokhonn, who began a two-day official visit to Malaysia today.

items.title: Loke resigns as Negeri Sembilan DAP chairman after state election defeat, stays on as party sec-gen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke today announced his resignation as Negeri Sembilan DAP chairman following Saturday’s outcome of the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election, in which he failed to retain the Chennah seat. ”I feel that the time has come for me to step down as state chairman and leave it to the Negeri Sembilan leadership and the Negeri Sembilan DAP committee to appoint and choose one of the existing committee members to become the new Negeri Sembilan chairman,” he said. Elaborating further, Loke said a Negeri Sembilan DAP committee meeting would be held soon to elect a new state chairman and leadership line-up.

items.title: DAP to put govt role to vote as delegates decide whether party stays until Parliament ends
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 4 — DAP will table a motion to decide if the party will remain in the government till the end of the current Parliament’s term at its National Convention on Aug 16. DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the matter was decided at the party’s central executive committee (CEC) meeting yesterday. DAP national chairman Gobind Singh Deo, DAP deputy secretary-general Hannah Yeoh and the party’s senior leadership attended the meeting.

items.title: First 2 deaths reported in US Cyclosporiasis outbreak
items.summary: LOS ANGELES: The US Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) on Monday confirmed the first two deaths linked to the country's cyclosporiasis outbreak, Xinhua reported. "CDC is aware of two cyclosporiasis-related deaths in people with underlying health conditions from Michigan as part of this outbreak," the CDC said in a notice, adding that it will update its website to include laboratory-confirmed cases, hospitalisations and deaths. State health officials said no additional information about the two cases would be released.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher against major currencies, nearly unchanged against greenback
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against other major currencies, and was almost unchanged versus the US dollar on Tuesday following the release of the US Institute for Supply Management (ISM) Manufacturing PMI data. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US ISM Manufacturing PMI surprised on the upside as the index rose to 55.6 points in July from the consensus estimate of 54.0 points, reinforcing expectations of a US interest rate hike. More to come © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Cargo vessel hit by 'unknown projectile' in Hormuz Strait
items.summary: DUBAI: A cargo vessel was struck by an "unknown projectile" in the Strait of Hormuz off the coast of Oman, a British maritime agency said on Tuesday, without providing details on damage or injuries. The vessel, which has not been named, reported being "hit by an unknown projectile", and authorities were investigating, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said. The incident occurred 20 nautical miles (37 kilometres) northeast of Al Khasab, Oman.

items.title: WHO demands protection for Gaza health care facilities amid israeli attacks
items.summary: GAZA CITY: The World Health Organisation (WHO) called on Monday for an immediate end to Israeli attacks on medical facilities in Gaza following a strike that destroyed a critical storage unit and essential supplies. "WHO calls for the protection of health care. Health care facilities must never be attacked or militarised," Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said in a statement, according to Anadolu Ajansi.

items.title: Identity politics claims just an excuse to hide defeat, Khaled tells PH leaders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A senior Umno leader has dismissed claims by Pakatan Harapan leaders suggesting that the Negri Sembilan election campaign was marred by racial identity politics. Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin told the New Straits Times that such claims were merely an excuse by PH leaders to cover up their defeat in the Aug 1 state election. "BN also fielded non-Malay candidates from MCA and MIC.

items.title: Two Pakistanis arrested in joint Singapore-Pakistan-Interpol cybercrime operation
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Two Pakistani nationals linked to the Tycoon2FA cybercrime syndicate were arrested in Pakistan following a joint operation by the Singapore Police Force (SPF), Pakistan's National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) and Interpol. In a statement on Monday, the SPF said Tycoon2FA is a phishing-as-a-service platform that provides subscribers with ready-made phishing infrastructure for a monthly fee, enabling cybercriminals to create fake websites to steal victims' credentials and gain unauthorised access to their accounts. The SPF said officers from its Cyber Command worked closely with the NCCIA and Interpol after investigating the cases, leading to the identification of the two Pakistani nationals believed to have developed Tycoon2FA.

items.title: KTMB extends Southern Shuttle service to Paloh from Aug 8
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) will extend its Southern Shuttle service on the Paloh-JB Sentral-Paloh route from Aug 8. KTMB said in a statement today that the expanded service will cover seven stations – Paloh, Kluang, Renggam, Layang-Layang, Kulai, Kempas Baru and JB Sentral – with the journey from Paloh to JB Sentral taking about 120 minutes. KTMB said the new service will operate 10 trips daily, comprising five services from Paloh to JB Sentral and five in the opposite direction, with each train accommodating up to 400 passengers.

items.title: [UPDATED] Five more Immigration officers arrested over hacking of MyIMMs, fraudulent PLKS
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission has arrested five more Immigration Department officers in the widening investigation into the alleged hacking of the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs) to issue fraudulent approval of Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS). The latest arrests are part of the ongoing Op Crack investigation, which has already seen several Immigration officers, company directors, foreigners and a police officer detained over alleged corruption and system breach. An MACC source said the five suspects, four men and a woman aged in their 30s and 40s, were arrested about 1pm yesterday when they turned up to have their statements recorded at MACC headquarters.

items.title: TikTok settling three teen social media lawsuits ahead of trial
items.summary: NEW YORK: TikTok has agreed to settle three lawsuits brought by young people who accuse social media companies of designing their platforms to be addictive and harming their mental health, a plaintiffs' lawyer said Monday. The cases are among thousands of similar lawsuits consolidated in California state court. The plaintiffs' claims against Meta Platforms, Google's YouTube and Snap Inc's Snapchat will continue.

items.title: What is a ‘new born child’? Malaysia’s Court of Appeal clarifies citizenship laws for abandoned children
items.summary: But what is a “new born child”? While agreeing that G was abandoned as a child, the court said Section 19B “does not apply to every abandoned child” as Section 19B also requires the child to also be “new born”. The court said it cannot remove the “new born” requirement from Section 19B.

items.title: US State Department to close consulates in Canada, Japan and Indonesia, sources say
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US State Department has notified Congress that it plans to close five foreign missions in a rare downsizing of America's global diplomatic footprint, according to people familiar with the notice. In the notice sent to some congressional committees late last week, the State Department said it planned to close its posts in St. George's, Grenada; Nagoya, Japan; Medan, Indonesia; Douala, Cameroon; and Winnipeg, Canada. The expected closures, which have not been previously reported, represent a rare example of the US closing multiple foreign missions in a downsizing that is not tied to a particular geopolitical event.

items.title: Spain defends Ceuta sovereignty after Moroccan migrant rush
items.summary: CEUTA: Spain on Monday insisted its sovereignty over Ceuta was "unquestionable", after tens of thousands of migrants irregularly entered the North African territory from Morocco in an unprecedented and deadly surge. Morocco does not recognise Ceuta and Madrid's other territory in North Africa, Melilla, as Spanish and has claimed sovereignty over them since its independence in 1956. The Spanish central government's delegate in Ceuta, Miguel Angel Perez, said Monday that 2,500 of them were estimated to still be in Ceuta.

items.title: Firefighters battle blaze near Sepang police station
items.summary: A FOREST fire covering 2.8ha, about the size of four football fields, broke out on hilly terrain near the Sepang district police headquarters early yesterday. "The fire was estimated to have spread across 2.8ha of hilly forest." "Firefighters from the Kuala Lumpur International Airport fire station, assisted by personnel from the Sepang Fire and Rescue Station, arrived at the scene at 1.48amm" it added.

items.title: Trump says Iran facing 'last chance before decapitation'
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Monday that negotiations with Iran were ongoing despite Teheran's denials and that the Islamic republic was facing a "last chance before decapitation". Iran's Foreign Ministry denied on Monday that negotiations with Washington were taking place, but Trump insisted they were. The talks are focused on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which Trump said could come "literally by tomorrow", and the denuclearisation of Iran, which he said could "take a little while".

items.title: North Korea condemns US and allies' cyber threat warning
items.summary: SEOUL: North Korea accused the United States and its allies of seeking to "tarnish the image" of the communist state after they warned against employing its IT workers, state media reported on Tuesday. The US and 10 Asian and European allies on Friday issued a joint statement saying North Korea was using skilled workers under false identities to fund its nuclear and ballistic missile programmes. An unnamed spokesman for the North Korean Foreign Ministry dismissed the joint warning as "a stereotyped political accusation with a sinister purpose to tarnish the image of our state", state news agency KCNA reported.

items.title: Kelantan police launch guidebook on tackling student issues
items.summary: A NEW police guide aims to improve how school liaison officers address social issues among students through more structured briefings. Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the initiative was discussed during a meeting with the state Education Department on improving information sharing between them. He said briefings would be conducted at suitable times, including during school hours, with content tailored to students' age groups and education levels.

items.title: Nestle Malaysia outpaces 2025 emissions target
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd has cut its greenhouse gas emissions by 31 per cent from its 2018 baseline. Nestle Malaysia said the achievement was driven by initiatives across its operations and supply chain. Nestle Malaysia chief executive officer Juan Aranols said the milestone reflects years of collaboration across the company's operations and value chain.

items.title: Trump attorney-general pick looks set to clear US Senate hurdle
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's former personal lawyer Todd Blanche appeared on track on Monday to become the next US attorney-general after two Republican senators dropped their opposition to his nomination. Blanche's Senate confirmation has been held up by concerns from Senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis over a US$1.8 billion fund for alleged victims of politically motivated prosecution and a tax audit immunity deal with the Republican president. Blanche issued a written order over the weekend scrapping the so-called "anti-weaponisation fund" and said the audit immunity agreement with Trump, his two eldest sons and the Trump Organization would apply only "retroactively" to past tax years and not future filings.

items.title: Trump says talks with Iran under way but Teheran denies any planned
items.summary: WASHINGTON/DUBAI: US President Donald Trump said on Monday that talks with Iran were under way, warning that it was a "last chance" for Teheran to sign a good deal to end the five-month-old war, but Iran denied that any negotiations were being held or planned. "This is a last chance for them (Iran) to sign a good document," he said. Earlier on Monday, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said no negotiations with the United States were taking place and no meetings were scheduled.

items.title: Australia confirms first mass death of seabirds from H5N1
items.summary: AUSTRALIA warned yesterday against the risk of a wider spread of H5N1 bird flu after its first mass mortality episode among seabirds killed about 50 greater crested terns off the coast south of Adelaide. Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said testing confirmed H5N1 bird flu in a group of 49 dead and 35 sick terns found by helicopter surveillance on rocks off Cape Jaffa, 250km from Adelaide last Friday. Australia's tally of 74 confirmed cases was spread as wide as the states of Western Australia and Queensland, though most cases were in South Australia, said Collins.

items.title: Aston Martin creditors threaten legal action over plan to sell branding rights
items.summary: The loss-making luxury carmaker secured £550 million (US$738.38 million) in debt financing in July, led by funds managed by BlackRock-owned HPS Investment Partners. The financing comprises a £450 million secured term loan, a £100 million delayed-draw term loan and a separate £100 million permitted debt-incurrence capacity. Aston Martin and HPS could not immediately be reached for comment outside regular business hours.

items.title: Death toll from Venezuela quakes rises past 6,000
items.summary: CARACAS: The twin quakes that shattered Venezuela in June killed 6,125 people, National Assembly Chief Jorge Rodriguez said on Monday. Local media quoted La Guaira Governor Jose Alejandro Teran as saying around 1,400 people remain missing after the disaster. Almost 24,000 people in La Guaira and Caracas are living in makeshift shelters following the earthquakes.

items.title: Man's body found floating in river wrapped in net
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: The body of a man believed to have been murdered was found floating in Sungai Tanjung Sembrong, Parit Raja, here yesterday. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrulanuar Mushaddat Abdullah Sani confirmed the discovery when contacted. He said a statement on the discovery would be issued by the Johor police headquarters.

items.title: Loke blames slander, personal attacks for Chennah defeat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke blamed personal attacks and slander as among the reasons for his failure to defend the Chennah seat in the Negri Sembilan election. He said unfounded allegations were seized upon by his opponents to fuel a false narrative. "And in Negri Sembilan, particularly in the villages, these whispers proved effective," he said.

items.title: Maran Umno Youth chief on the way home from family getaway before accident
items.summary: TEMERLOH: Maran Umno Youth chief Mohd Radzi Rahimi took part in a motorcycle convoy in Pulau Pangkor, Perak, before going on a family holiday to Genting Highlands yesterday. His father, Rahimi Abd Samad, 63, said his eldest of four children travelled to Pulau Pangkor with his wife, Nuraini Mohammad Jafri, 36, and their 5-year-old twin sons last Thursday. Rahimi said he was told that Radzi's wife, brother-in-law Mohammad Nizam Mohammad Jafri, and their sons travelled to Pangkor in a pick-up truck, while Radzi rode his motorcycle with the rest of the convoy.

items.title: When rogue AI launches a cyberattack, who is legally responsible?
items.summary: RECENT cyberattacks carried out autonomously by two rogue OpenAI artificial intelligence (AI) models raises an untested legal question: who is responsible when AI acts on its own? In the middle of last month, two OpenAI models undergoing testing left their confined environment — a scenario the developers had not anticipated — and ventured onto the Internet, where they attacked Hugging Face, an AI model-hosting platform. "If a human OpenAI employee had broken into Hugging Face's systems... OpenAI would be liable for the employee's wrongful conduct," University of Houston law professor Gabriel Weil wrote in an opinion piece for the Transformer newsletter.

items.title: OPEC+ oil output hike is irrelevant for now, not for later
items.summary: The seven members of OPEC+ undertaking voluntary output cuts — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman — agreed at a meeting on Sunday to increase production by 188,000 barrels per day (bpd) for September. For the moment it matters little what the production quotas are, with the latest data from a Reuters survey showing the eight members of OPEC with quotas pumped 20.276 million bpd in June, which was 6.246 million bpd below the agreed target. Russia, the main non-OPEC member of the wider OPEC+ group, had production of 8.928 million bpd in June, according to OPEC data, which was almost one million bpd below its agreed quota.

items.title: Three Malaysians arrested in Hat Yai with RM4.3mil worth of syabu
items.summary: A Thai police spokesman said the suspects were arrested at Hat Yai railway station during a joint operation involving Hat Yai police's narcotics suppression unit, the railway police, the tourist police and the Region 9 Office of the Narcotics Control Board. The spokesman said the suspects were travelling from Bangkok to Hat Yai when police intercepted and searched them. "Officers found crystal methamphetamine, or syabu, concealed in three wheeled suitcases and three backpacks," the spokesman said.

items.title: Indonesian authorities put out airport video of Malaysian pilot allegedly smuggling 25kg ecstasy
items.summary: JAKARTA, Aug 3 — Indonesia’s Directorate General of Customs and Excise (Bea Cukai) has released CCTV footage showing the movements of a Malaysian pilot arrested last week over the alleged smuggling of about 25 kilogrammes of ecstasy through Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport. The video, uploaded on Bea Cukai’s official Instagram account on Monday, shows the 39-year-old suspect, dressed in a pilot’s uniform, collecting a large silver hard-shell suitcase from the baggage carousel while pulling a second black suitcase before walking through the arrival hall towards the customs clearance area. Close-up footage shows customs officers examining and removing the packages from the suitcase while the suspect is questioned during the inspection.

items.title: Maran Umno Youth chief, wife and child among four killed in Bentong crash
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 3 — Maran Umno Youth chief Mohd Radzi Rahimi died alongside his wife, child, and brother-in-law in a car accident in Bentong on Monday. The family was travelling in a four-wheel-drive vehicle along Jalan Lama Bentong when a massive tree collapsed, crushing the vehicle and killing four of its occupants.. “I am deeply saddened to receive news of the passing of the late Edy, Maran Umno Youth chief, together with his wife, child and brother-in-law, who were killed in an accident in Bentong.

items.title: Police question 10 individuals over deaths of two teen girls in Ipoh
items.summary: LARUT, Aug 3 — Police have recorded statements from 10 individuals to assist investigations into the deaths of two female students whose bodies were found at the Sungai Pari flats in Ipoh on July 24. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said those questioned included the victims’ friends and teachers. So far, our investigation has found no evidence of foul play,” he told reporters at the Selama district police headquarters today.

items.title: MACC officer rejects bias claim in Lim Guan Eng undersea tunnel probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — A Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigating officer today denied that his investigation into the RM6.3 billion Penang undersea tunnel and major roads project involving former Chief Minister Lim Guan Eng was conducted in a biased manner. Senior Superintendent Zulhilmi Ramli, 34, of the MACC Investigation Division at its headquarters, rejected the suggestion during cross-examination by defence lawyer Mohd Haijan Omar at Lim’s corruption trial. Earlier, Mohd Haijan questioned why investigators had not verified whether Consortium Zenith Beijing Urban Construction Group (CZBUCG) had submitted any claim to the Penang government for the feasibility study and detailed design (FSDD) relating to the undersea tunnel project.

items.title: ‘Slander and forgery’: Warisan denies fake letter claiming unity government exit
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 3 — Parti Warisan (Warisan) has strongly denied a viral social media claim alleging that the party has decided to withdraw from the Unity Government. Meanwhile, Deputy Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Dr Mohammad Yusof Apdal also confirmed that the document titled “Parti WARISAN Menarik Diri Daripada Kerajaan Perpaduan” (Parti Warisan Withdraws from the Unity Government) is fake. Mohammad Yusof stressed that any official position or decision by Warisan would only be communicated through the party’s official communication channels and authorised leaders.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines pilot’s baggage raised no alarm at KLIA before drug arrest in Jakarta, border agency chief says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — Malaysian authorities are examining how a pilot arrested with drugs at an Indonesian airport passed through security screening at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) without his baggage being flagged, according to The Star . Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said checks confirmed that the pilot underwent all required screening before boarding the aircraft on July 28. Mohd Shuhaily said the screening system combined artificial intelligence with human assessment, with the scanner assigning a risk level to baggage before security personnel decided whether further inspection was required.

items.title: Defence claims celebrity preacher Da’i Syed conviction unsafe, insists victim’s actions pointed to consent
items.summary: Lawyer Datuk M M Athimulan, representing Da’i Syed, submitted that the prosecution’s own evidence disclosed numerous circumstances indicating that the sexual intercourse between the appellant and the victim was consensual. Athimulan said the Sessions Court had subsequently acquitted and discharged Da’i Syed, whose real name is Syed Shah Iqmal Syed Mohd Shaiful, at the close of the prosecution’s case without calling for his defence. The appellant was later convicted by another Sessions Court judge.

items.title: Selangor MB urges humane stray-dog enforcement after Rocky’s death
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has called for stray-dog enforcement to be carried out without cruelty, saying authorities must balance animal welfare with public safety following the death of a dog named Rocky during a Klang council operation. Amirudin said the operation in Taman Teluk Gedung Indah on July 29 was conducted by the Klang Royal City Council, or MBDK, following complaints from the public. “The authorities take action based on complaints involving stray dogs.

items.title: Fire Department warns Kelantan at greater risk of destructive blazes under Super El Niño
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 3 — The Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) expects the Super El Niño phenomenon, forecast to peak towards the end of this year, to increase the risk of fires in the state due to hotter and drier weather, while significantly reducing the likelihood of major floods this year. Its director, Farhan Sufyan Borhan said the state could face a fairly severe drought, and advised the public not to carry out open burning, which could trigger fires, adding that the department had received 2,197 fire-related emergency calls from January until now, compared with 373 calls recorded throughout last year, making Kelantan the second-highest state for open fires after Kedah. Yesterday, media reported that Kedah, Perlis and Kelantan are among the states most likely to face severe drought conditions when the Super El Niño is expected to reach its peak later this year.

items.title: Deputy minister says Social Work Council coming once new Act officially takes effect
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Aug 3 — The Malaysian Social Work Profession Council will be established soon after the Social Work Profession Act comes into force, said Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying. She said the ministry was currently proceeding with the gazettement process for the Social Work Profession Act following the passing of the bill by both the Dewan Rakyat and Dewan Negara. “The Social Work Profession Bill was passed by the Dewan Rakyat and we are also grateful that it was passed by the Dewan Negara last week.

items.title: Education Minister Fadhlina vows stronger psychosocial support after Selangor teacher’s tragic death
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — The Education Ministry is making every effort to ensure that psychosocial support for the school community is strengthened following the recent death of a female teacher in Selangor. Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said she understands the concerns among educators and the public over the incident, which she described as being particularly close to her heart, as she began her political journey as a mental health activist. She said the ministry has always prioritised the mental well-being of the education community through collaboration with non-governmental organisations (NGOs), the Health Ministry and counsellors.

items.title: Perak police chief: Fugitive wanted over knife attack on two cops dies after being shot during arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — A suspect wanted over a knife attack that injured two police officers in Perak died after being shot when he allegedly charged at another police team with a machete during an attempt to arrest him. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said a team from the Selama district police headquarters, led by Inspector B. Thanabalan, went to the hut to arrest the man. Police then sought medical assistance from Selama district hospital.

items.title: Indonesian mother, Bangladeshi partner face murder charge in Penang over death of five‑year‑old son
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 3 — An Indonesian woman and her Bangladeshi boyfriend were charged in the Magistrate’s Court today with the murder of a five-year-old boy last month. Dina Hayati, 30, and Sany nodded in understanding after the charge was read before Magistrate Noor Idayu Salim. No plea was recorded, however, as the case falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.

items.title: MAHB pledges full support, vows tighter airport security after pilot’s Indonesia drug arrest
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 3 — Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) today reaffirmed its commitment to supporting multi-agency efforts to safeguard Malaysia’s borders against illegal activities, including through close cooperation with enforcement authorities following the recent drug-related case involving a Malaysian pilot in Indonesia. “MAHB remains committed to supporting these multi-agency efforts to safeguard Malaysia’s borders against illegal activities and will provide any assistance required in relation to this case,” MAHB said. MAHB clarified that its Aviation Security (AVSEC) team is primarily responsible for preventing acts of unlawful interference that may jeopardise the security and safety of civil aviation and air transport.

items.title: Four killed, child injured after tree crushes Ford Raptor in Bentong
items.summary: Bentong district police chief Superintendent Zaiham Mohd Kahar said the police received information about the incident from the public at about 12.30pm. He said all the victims were in the Ford Raptor vehicle at the time of the incident. He said another five-year-old boy who was in the back seat was injured and sent to Bentong Hospital for treatment.

items.title: Defence Minister Khaled confirms US pledge to deepen Malaysia cooperation at military conference
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — The United States (US) is committed to continuing to strengthen close ties with Malaysia, including in the defence sector, said Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin. Apart from Kevin, Mohamed Khaled also received courtesy calls from Asean Secretary-General Dr Kao Kim Hourn and Singapore’s Permanent Secretary for the Ministry of Defence Joseph Leong. He said they also agreed that the defence sector has an important role in supporting Asean’s goals and strengthening cooperation between member states.

items.title: Najib in the dock: High Court hears betrayal of rakyat in alleged US$5.64b 1MDB fraud
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — The High Court heard today that 1MDB and its four subsidiaries are set to prove that former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak stood at the very heart of the alleged fraud that cost the sovereign wealth fund US$5.64 billion. Reading the plaintiffs’ opening statement, counsel Datuk Lim Chee Wee said they would establish that Najib wielded immense control over 1MDB’s management. They named Najib; former 1MDB finance director Terrence Geh Choh Heng; former counsel Jasmine Loo Ai Swan; former executive director Casey Tang Keng Chee; former chief investment officer Vincent Beng Huat Koh; former chief operating officer Radhi Mohamad; former investment director Kelvin Tan Kay Jim; and former chief investment officer Nik Faisal Ariff Kamil, as defendants.

items.title: Klang council denies SOP breach during stray dog-catching operation, says animal died in struggle with resident
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — Klang’s city council has denied breaching standard operating procedures during a stray dog-catching operation that left one animal dead, saying the dog became strangled during a struggle involving a resident who claimed to be its owner. Klang Royal City Council mayor Datuk Abd Hamid Hussain said officers had followed procedures set by the Housing and Local Government Ministry during the operation at Taman Teluk Gedung Indah last week. He said, however, that the person later denied owning the animal.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh vows ecological buffer, rediscovered fireflies drive 300‑metre protection at Bukit Kiara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — The government is engaging with landowners surrounding Bukit Kiara to implement a previously announced 300-metre ecological buffer zone to protect a rare firefly species recently rediscovered in the federal park. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said discussions with the affected stakeholders were ongoing following Kuala Lumpur City Hall’s (DBKL) announcement of its plan to establish the buffer zone around Bukit Kiara. Hannah said the buffer zone was intended to safeguard the habitat while discussions with developers continued to find a practical solution.

items.title: Lorry driver and wife plead not guilty as Melaka court hears child abuse charges
items.summary: The accused were charged separately before Judge Rohatul Akmar Abdullah. items.title: Singaporean biker killed, two fellow riders hurt in crash involving Toyota Vellfire on North-South Expressway near Kulai
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — A 56-year-old Singaporean motorcyclist was killed and two Malaysian riders injured in a four-vehicle crash on the North-South Expressway near Kulai yesterday. Kulai district police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee said preliminary investigations found that the three riders — the Singaporean and two Malaysians aged 57 and 39 — were travelling south when the crash occurred. “The incident also involved the other two motorcyclists.

items.title: MetMalaysia alert: Torrential rain, lightning and gusty winds batter states from Kedah to Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds expected to affect eight states and the Federal Territory of Labuan until 6pm today. It said in a statement that the adverse weather is forecast to affect Sik and Baling in Kedah; Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim in Perak; Jeli, Bachok and Pasir Puteh in Kelantan; and Besut, Setiu and Hulu Terengganu in Terengganu. In Sarawak and Sarawak, the affected areas are Kuching (Bau), Sri Aman, Betong (Pusa and Betong), Sarikei (Pakan, Julau and Meradong), Sibu and Kapit (Song and Kapit), and the Interior (Sipitang, Tenom, Kuala Penyu, Beaufort, Keningau and Tambunan), the West Coast and Kudat (Kota Marudu).

items.title: State Speaker: Selangor assembly reviewing all lawmakers after bankruptcy disqualification claim
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 3 — The Selangor state assembly is reviewing the status of all its members after claims that one assemblyman may have been disqualified over bankruptcy, Utusan Malaysia reported today. State assembly Speaker Lau Weng San said he could not yet confirm the identity of the lawmaker concerned because checks and investigations were still under way. Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari previously said the matter would be determined by Lau before the Election Commission (EC) was informed.
